title: Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 — Section 5 (Extent of judicial intervention)

content.overview: Section 5 establishes limited judicial intervention in matters governed by Part I: judicial authorities shall not intervene except where the Act itself provides for intervention.
content.glance: No court intervention in Part I matters except where Part I expressly provides a gateway.
content.study: Section 5 begins with a non obstante clause. Identify whether Part I governs the matter, then identify the exact Part I provision authorising the requested judicial action. General powers under other laws cannot bypass the Part I scheme.

sections.heading: Non-intervention starting point
sections.body: Notwithstanding other law, judicial intervention is excluded in matters governed by Part I except where Part I provides for it.

sections.heading: Part I field of operation
sections.body: Confirm the matter is governed by Part I before applying section 5.

sections.heading: Statutory gateway
sections.body: Intervention is lawful only where a specific Part I provision authorises the requested judicial action.

sections.heading: Relationship with other laws
sections.body: The non obstante clause prevents using another law as an independent intervention route contrary to Part I.

examples.title: Authorised intervention
examples.body: A party seeks a remedy that Part I expressly assigns to a court. Section 5 does not bar it.

examples.title: No Part I gateway
examples.body: A party asks a court to intervene without identifying a Part I authorising provision. Section 5 bars the request.

hypotheticals.question: Does section 5 mean courts never act in arbitration?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Part I itself provides specified judicial functions. Section 5 limits intervention to those gateways.

rows.left: Intervention only where Part I provides

misconceptions.trap: Courts can never intervene in arbitration.
misconceptions.correction: Intervention remains available where Part I expressly provides for it.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What is the section 5 test?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Identify whether Part I governs the matter and the Part I provision authorising the intervention. If none, section 5 bars it.

examTips: Do not describe s. 5 as absolute ouster.
